trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Barcelona
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Barcelona Airport at 13:00. Take the Aerobus (€6.75 one-way) or Metro L9 Sud (€5.15) to the city center. Check in to Barcelona Boutique Stay in Eixample. Once settled, take a self-guided walk along Passeig de Gràcia to admire the iconic modernista facades — spot Casa Batlló and Casa Milà (La Pedrera) from the outside for free. Stroll through the Eixample grid streets and soak in the Art Nouveau architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the lively Gràcia neighborhood (15-min walk from Eixample) to explore Plaça del Sol and Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia. Grab dinner at a local tapas bar and enjoy the vibrant street atmosphere. As the night picks up, check out Bar Calders or a nearby terrace bar for affordable drinks and to mingle with locals.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and croissant at the airport or skip — you arrive at 13:00
meals.lunch: Pick up a bocadillo (sandwich) or grab a menú del día at a local café near the hotel for €10–13
meals.dinner: Tapas at a budget bar in Gràcia — patatas bravas, pan con tomate, croquetas. Budget €12–16 per person including a drink

day_by_day.notes: Get a T-Casual metro card (10 trips, ~€12.15) at the airport or any metro station — it will save money throughout the trip. August is hot in Barcelona (30°C+), so carry water. Check in is typically from 14:00 or 15:00 — confirm with the hotel in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with breakfast near the hotel, then head to the Sagrada Família (metro L2/L5 to Sagrada Família stop). Book tickets online in advance to save time — entry is €26 but it's the unmissable architectural centerpiece of Barcelona. Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring Gaudí's extraordinary basilica inside and out.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take the metro to Park Güell (bus 24 or metro L3 to Lesseps, then walk). The monumental zone requires a ticket (~€10, book online), but the surrounding park is free and offers stunning city views. Spend the afternoon exploring the park, the dragon staircase, and the mosaic terrace. Afterward, descend back toward Gràcia for a rest at the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Gothic Quarter (El Gòtic) — take the metro L3 to Liceu. Wander the narrow medieval streets, visit Plaça Reial (free), and admire the Barcelona Cathedral exterior. The Gothic Quarter comes alive at night with street musicians and affordable bars. Head to a bar on Carrer dels Escudellers or Plaça George Orwell (known as Plaça del Trippy) for budget-friendly nightlife.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and toast with tomato (pa amb tomàquet) at a local café near the hotel — €3–5
meals.lunch: Menú del día near Park Güell or in Gràcia — a 3-course meal with drink for €11–14
meals.dinner: Budget pintxos or tapas in the Gothic Quarter — many bars offer pintxos from €1.50 each. Budget €10–15 including drinks

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família and Park Güell tickets online well in advance — they sell out, especially in August. Wear comfortable shoes for Park Güell's uphill walk. Stay hydrated in the summer heat.

day_by_day.morning: Head to the El Born / Sant Pere neighborhood (metro L4 to Barceloneta or Jaume I). Visit the Basílica de Santa Maria del Mar — a stunning 14th-century Gothic church that is free to enter in the morning. Explore the charming El Born streets and browse the boutiques and street art. Visit the Mercat de Santa Caterina (a colorful alternative to La Boqueria, less touristy and free to browse).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down to Barceloneta Beach (free) — Barcelona's most central beach. Spend the early afternoon swimming and relaxing on the Mediterranean coast. Walk along the Passeig Marítim promenade and explore the Port Olímpic area. Visit the iconic Frank Gehry golden fish sculpture (free). Head back to the hotel in the late afternoon to freshen up.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Barcelona's legendary nightlife. The city doesn't get going until late — dinner at 21:00–22:00, clubs open around midnight. Start with pre-drinks at a rooftop bar or terrace in Eixample. Head to the Eixample Esquerra area (known as Gayxample but welcoming to all) for vibrant bar-hopping. Clubs like Sala Apolo (Carrer Nou de la Rambla) open late and often have affordable entry before 01:00.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a café in El Born — coffee and a pastry for €3–5
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood or a bocadillo at a chiringuito (beach bar) on Barceloneta — budget €8–12
meals.dinner: Pre-nightlife dinner at a budget restaurant in Eixample — pizza, pasta, or a set menu for €10–15

day_by_day.notes: Barcelona nightlife runs very late — clubs peak between 02:00 and 05:00. Many venues offer free or discounted entry before 01:00 or with a flyer/app deal. Check Resident Advisor or Xceed app for free/cheap event listings. Lockers at the beach (€3–5) are useful if you bring valuables.

day_by_day.morning: After a late night, start slow. Late breakfast or brunch near the hotel. Once refreshed, visit the Palau de la Música Catalana in El Born — the exterior is a UNESCO-listed modernista masterpiece and free to admire. If budget allows, a guided tour is ~€22 but the exterior alone is worth the visit. Explore the surrounding Sant Pere neighborhood streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the metro or bus to Montjuïc hill. Take the Montjuïc cable car (~€12.70 return) or the cheaper option — bus 150 from Plaça Espanya (included in T-Casual card). Visit the Fundació Joan Miró (€14 entry — worth it for art/architecture lovers) or simply enjoy the free gardens, the Olympic Stadium exterior, and panoramic city views. Walk down through the gardens or take the cable car back.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Magic Fountain of Montjuïc (Font Màgica) — a free spectacular light and music show held on Thursday–Sunday evenings (check 2027 schedule, typically starts at 21:30 in summer). Afterward, head to the Poble Sec neighborhood at the foot of Montjuïc — one of Barcelona's most authentic and affordable nightlife areas. Bar hop along Carrer de Blai, famous for its cheap pintxos bars.

meals.breakfast: Late brunch at a café near the hotel — eggs, toast, juice for €6–9
meals.lunch: Picnic on Montjuïc — grab supplies from a Mercadona or Lidl supermarket (€4–7) for a budget-friendly meal with a view
meals.dinner: Pintxos crawl on Carrer de Blai in Poble Sec — pintxos from €1–2 each, budget €10–15 for a full dinner with drinks

day_by_day.notes: Check the Font Màgica official schedule before going — it operates on specific days and times in summer 2027. Poble Sec is an up-and-coming neighborhood with great value bars and restaurants — a favorite among locals. Montjuïc gardens are free and offer shade — great for a hot August afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — visit La Boqueria Market on La Rambla (free to enter, but buy snacks/fruit rather than full meals to stay on budget). Walk the full length of La Rambla from Plaça de Catalunya to the Columbus Monument (free). Visit the MACBA (Museum of Contemporary Art) — the Richard Meier building itself is an architectural gem. Entry is €12, or admire the exterior and the lively skate plaza for free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Eixample for a final architecture walk — seek out lesser-known modernista gems like Casa Lleó Morera, Casa Amatller, and the Palau del Baró de Quadras (all free to view from outside). Visit the Mercat de l'Abaceria in Gràcia (free) for local atmosphere. Do any last-minute souvenir shopping at budget stores on Carrer del Consell de Cent or at El Corte Inglés sale sections. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a beloved local restaurant in Eixample — splurge slightly on your last night with a proper Catalan meal. Try escalivada, fideuà, or crema catalana for dessert. Enjoy a final passeig (evening stroll) along Passeig de Gràcia, lit up beautifully at night, and take in the illuminated facades of the modernista buildings one last time.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and croissant at a café on La Rambla or nearby — €3–5
meals.lunch: Fresh fruit, jamón, and cheese from La Boqueria for a picnic — €6–10
meals.dinner: Farewell Catalan dinner at a mid-range local restaurant — budget €18–25 per person for a special last meal with wine

day_by_day.notes: Keep transport costs in mind for departure day — Aerobus or metro to the airport. Store luggage at the hotel until departure if your flight is in the evening. La Boqueria is very touristy — buy fruit or snacks but avoid the overpriced seafood stalls at the front. The back stalls have much better prices.

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Barcelona Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to Barcelona Boutique Stay in Eixample district (~30–40 min by Aerobus or taxi). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented in the neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll along Passeig de Gràcia to admire the famous 'Block of Discord' — see Casa Batlló and Casa Amatller from the outside at no cost. Get your bearings in Eixample and pick up a city map or download offline navigation. Pop into a local café for a welcome coffee and snack.
day_by_day.evening: Barceloneta Beach Sunset & Chiringuito Experience — take the metro (L4) down to Barceloneta Beach (~15 min from Eixample). Arrive in time for the golden-hour sunset over the Mediterranean. Grab drinks and tapas at a chiringuito beachfront bar. Enjoy a relaxed first evening soaking in the atmosphere without overdoing it after travel.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a light snack on the plane/airport — arrival is at 13:00
meals.lunch: Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca (Eixample) — excellent tapas and montaditos, mid-range, ~€15–20 per person
meals.dinner: La Cova Fumada or a chiringuito at Barceloneta Beach — fresh seafood and cold beers by the water, ~€20–30 per person

day_by_day.notes: August in Barcelona is hot and humid (expect 28–33°C). Pack light clothes and sunscreen. Buy a T-Casual 10-trip metro card upon arrival to save on transport costs throughout the trip. Eixample is very walkable and well-connected to all key areas.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour — book the first available morning slot (9:00 or 9:30 AM). The basilica is just a 10-minute walk from most of Eixample. A guided tour (~90 min) reveals Gaudí's genius across the Nativity and Passion facades, the forest-like interior, and the towers. Book tickets online in advance to avoid queues.
day_by_day.afternoon: Parc de la Ciutadella & Born Gothic Architecture Walk — take the metro (L4) to Ciutadella/Vila Olímpica. Explore the monumental cascade fountain and lush parkland of Parc de la Ciutadella, then wander into the El Born neighborhood. Discover the Gothic and medieval architecture of Carrer del Montcada, the Basílica de Santa Maria del Mar, and the narrow medieval lanes.
day_by_day.evening: Explore El Born's vibrant bar scene for pre-dinner drinks — the neighborhood is packed with atmospheric cocktail bars and wine bars. Head to a traditional Catalan restaurant in El Born for dinner, then take the metro back to Eixample.

meals.breakfast: Federal Café in Sant Antoni (near Eixample) — excellent brunch spot with avocado toast, eggs, and specialty coffee, ~€10–14 per person
meals.lunch: Bar del Pla in El Born — classic Catalan tapas in a lively setting, ~€15–22 per person
meals.dinner: El Xampanyet in El Born — legendary cava bar and tapas restaurant, very atmospheric, ~€20–28 per person

day_by_day.notes: Pre-booking Sagrada Família tickets online is essential — they sell out days or weeks in advance in August. Add-on tower access for panoramic views is highly recommended (small extra fee). Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Born Gothic walk — cobblestones can be uneven.

day_by_day.morning: Seafood Paella Cooking Class & Market Tour — join a local chef for a guided visit to La Boqueria Market on La Rambla, selecting fresh ingredients. Then head to the cooking school kitchen to learn authentic seafood paella from scratch. Classes typically run 10:00 AM–1:30 PM and include eating the meal you cook.
day_by_day.afternoon: After your cooking class lunch, take a leisurely walk through the Gothic Quarter (Barri Gòtic) — explore the Barcelona Cathedral, Plaça Reial, and the hidden Roman ruins. Browse independent boutiques and souvenir shops. Rest back at the hotel during the hottest part of the afternoon (3:00–5:00 PM) — this is very typical and advisable in August.
day_by_day.evening: Beachfront Nightclub Experience at Opium or Pacha — get ready at the hotel and head to the Passeig Marítim. Start with dinner or drinks at a beachfront restaurant around 9:00–10:00 PM (dinner is eaten late in Barcelona). Clubs typically open around midnight and peak at 1:00–3:00 AM. Dress smart-casual; expect a €15–20 entry fee often including a drink.

meals.breakfast: Hofmann Pastisseria in Eixample or a local neighborhood bakery — fresh croissants, pa amb tomàquet (bread with tomato), and coffee, ~€6–9 per person
meals.lunch: Included in the cooking class — the paella you prepare with the chef
meals.dinner: Chiringuito Escribà on Barceloneta or a beachfront restaurant on Passeig Marítim before the club — seafood and cocktails, ~€25–35 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class in advance as spots fill quickly in summer. Nightclub tip: avoid going before midnight — clubs are empty before then. Keep an eye on your belongings on La Rambla, which is known for pickpockets. Stay hydrated throughout the day — August heat is intense.

day_by_day.morning: Late, relaxed start after the nightclub evening — sleep in until 9:30–10:00 AM. Visit the Fundació Antoni Tàpies in Eixample (5-min walk from the hotel) — a stunning modernista building housing contemporary Catalan art. Alternatively, explore the lesser-known Palau del Baró de Quadras or admire the exterior of Casa Lleó Morera for more architecture gems.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the metro or a scenic walk up to Gràcia neighborhood — explore Plaça del Sol and Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia, the bohemian local market Mercat de l'Abaceria, and the colorful Parc Güell (book timed entry online in advance). Gaudí's mosaic terraces and the Hypostyle Room offer incredible architecture and panoramic city views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Eixample and explore the Esquerra de l'Eixample (left side of Eixample), known locally as the 'Gayxample' — a vibrant, inclusive neighborhood packed with excellent cocktail bars, terrace restaurants, and live music venues. Enjoy a relaxed evening bar-hopping or settle in for a long Catalan dinner.

meals.breakfast: Brunch at home base — try Parking Pizza or Syra Coffee in Eixample for a slow, late morning meal, ~€10–15 per person
meals.lunch: La Pepita in Gràcia — creative montaditos and craft beers in a charming space, ~€14–20 per person
meals.dinner: Bodega Sepúlveda in Eixample Esquerra — beloved neighborhood wine bar with excellent Catalan dishes and affordable wine list, ~€22–30 per person

day_by_day.notes: Parc Güell timed entry tickets must be booked online — the free outer zone is accessible without a ticket but the monumental zone (terraces and Hypostyle Room) requires a reservation. Go early afternoon (around 5:00 PM) to avoid peak heat. Gràcia is best explored on foot.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — visit the Recinte Modernista de Sant Pau, one of Barcelona's most underrated architectural masterpieces by Lluís Domènech i Montaner (a UNESCO World Heritage Site). It's just a 10-minute walk from Sagrada Família and far less crowded. The ornate Modernista pavilions and gardens are stunning in morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Passeig de Gràcia for last-minute souvenir shopping and a proper look inside Casa Batlló or La Pedrera (Casa Milà) — choose one for a ticketed interior visit (~€25–30 per person). Both offer spectacular Gaudí interiors and rooftop terraces. End with a final walk through Eixample to soak in the neighborhood one last time.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a rooftop restaurant or a classic Catalan restaurant in Eixample. Enjoy a final glass of cava or a vermouth at a local bar before packing up for departure.

meals.breakfast: Forn de Sant Jaume or any local forn (bakery) in Eixample — traditional Catalan pastries and café amb llet (coffee with milk), ~€5–8 per person
meals.lunch: Cervecería Catalana (revisit a favorite) or Taktika Berri — excellent Basque pintxos bar in Eixample, ~€15–22 per person
meals.dinner: Parking Pizza Eixample or Moments at Mandarin Oriental for a splurge-worthy farewell meal — budget accordingly, ~€25–50 per person depending on choice

day_by_day.notes: Check flight departure time and plan accordingly — if flying out on the 19th evening, skip the rooftop dinner and head to the airport by early evening. Barcelona El Prat Airport is 30–40 min from Eixample via Aerobus (departs from Plaça Catalunya). Leave extra time in August due to high-season airport congestion. Confirm hotel checkout time in advance.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Hotel Check-In: Flight LH lands at 13:00, so morning is in transit. Transfer from Barcelona El Prat Airport to Barcelona Boutique Stay in Eixample via private luxury transfer (pre-booked black car service). Check in, freshen up, and settle into your suite.
day_by_day.afternoon: Eixample Architecture Stroll & Passeig de Gràcia Exploration: After settling in, take a leisurely walk along Passeig de Gràcia — the luxury boulevard steps from your hotel. Admire the iconic 'Block of Discord' featuring Casa Batlló and Casa Amatller. Consider a self-guided or private guide tour of Casa Batlló's interior (book in advance). Browse the flagship luxury boutiques along the way.
day_by_day.evening: Barceloneta Beach Sunset & Chiringuito Experience: Head down to Barceloneta Beach for the golden-hour sunset over the Mediterranean. Enjoy cocktails at one of the upscale beachfront chiringuitos such as La Cova Fumada or Chiringuito Escribà. Soak in the warm August evening atmosphere as the city comes alive.

meals.breakfast: In transit / light airport lounge dining at Barcelona El Prat (Terminal 1 VIP Lounge)
meals.lunch: Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca — a beloved Eixample institution serving premium tapas and fresh seafood; perfect for a first taste of Barcelona after check-in
meals.dinner: Parking Pizza or upgrade to Bodega Sepúlveda for a relaxed premium dinner near the hotel, or dine at the beachfront restaurant Bestial near Barceloneta for Mediterranean cuisine with sea views

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange your private airport transfer before departure. Casa Batlló tickets should be booked online in advance — the Magic Nights evening experience is spectacular in summer. August evenings in Barcelona are warm (25–30°C), so light linen clothing is ideal.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour: Start the day with a premium guided tour of Gaudí's legendary unfinished basilica. Book a private guide for an in-depth exploration of the Nativity and Passion facades, the forest-like interior nave, and the tower lifts for panoramic city views. Arrive early (9:00 AM) to beat the crowds — the Sagrada Família is just a short taxi or metro ride from Eixample.
day_by_day.afternoon: Seafood Paella Cooking Class & Boqueria Market Tour: Join a local chef for an immersive culinary experience starting with a guided tour of La Boqueria Market to hand-select the freshest seafood, vegetables, and saffron. Then head to a premium cooking studio to master authentic Catalan seafood paella. This half-day class includes wine pairing and a sit-down lunch of your own creation.
day_by_day.evening: Beachfront Nightclub Experience at Opium or Pacha: Experience Barcelona's world-renowned nightlife at Opium Mar or Pacha Barcelona along Passeig Marítim. Arrange VIP table service in advance for the full premium experience. Barcelona nightlife starts late — arrive around midnight for peak atmosphere. Enjoy bottle service, international DJs, and the electric beachfront energy.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast at the boutique stay or head to Federal Café in Eixample for a gourmet brunch spread with specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Included as part of the Paella Cooking Class — a sit-down meal of your freshly prepared paella with Catalan wines
meals.dinner: Tickets Bar by Albert Adrià (reserve weeks in advance) for avant-garde tapas, or Bodega 1900 for elevated traditional vermouth and pintxos before heading to the club

day_by_day.notes: Sagrada Família tower lift tickets sell out fast — book the full guided experience with tower access well in advance. For Opium or Pacha, contact the venue's VIP concierge or use your hotel concierge to arrange table reservations. Clubs don't peak until 1–2 AM in Barcelona.

day_by_day.morning: Parc de la Ciutadella & Born Gothic Architecture Walk: After a leisurely late morning start (accounting for the previous night's late evening), explore the verdant Parc de la Ciutadella. Marvel at the monumental Cascade Fountain — a masterpiece co-designed by a young Gaudí — and stroll through the botanical gardens. Transition into the El Born neighborhood for a curated Gothic architecture walk through medieval streets, the stunning Santa Maria del Mar basilica, and the Palau de la Música Catalana exterior.
day_by_day.afternoon: Palau de la Música Catalana Guided Tour & Gràcia Neighborhood Exploration: Book a guided tour of the UNESCO-listed Palau de la Música Catalana, a breathtaking Modernista concert hall by Lluís Domènech i Montaner. Afterward, take a taxi up to the charming Gràcia neighborhood to explore its bohemian plazas, boutique design shops, and street art — a quieter, more local side of Barcelona.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Cocktails at a Rooftop Bar & Fine Dining: Head to the rooftop bar at the Hotel Arts Barcelona or the Mandarin Oriental's Terrat rooftop for panoramic sunset cocktails over the city skyline and sea. Follow with a reservation at one of Barcelona's Michelin-starred restaurants for an unforgettable dinner.

meals.breakfast: Room service or a slow breakfast at Syra Coffee or Nomad Coffee in El Born — among Barcelona's finest specialty coffee roasters
meals.lunch: El Xampanyet in El Born — a legendary cava bar serving charcuterie, anchovies, and Catalan classics with sparkling cava; an authentic local institution
meals.dinner: Disfrutar (2 Michelin stars) or Lasarte (3 Michelin stars) — two of Barcelona's finest fine-dining experiences offering avant-garde tasting menus with wine pairings; reservations essential months in advance

day_by_day.notes: Given the late night on Day 2, plan a flexible mid-morning start around 10:30–11:00 AM. The Palau de la Música Catalana tour must be pre-booked. If Disfrutar or Lasarte are unavailable, Cinc Sentits or Moments are excellent Michelin-starred alternatives in Eixample.

day_by_day.morning: Park Güell Private Early Access & Carmel Bunkers Viewpoint: Secure a timed-entry ticket for Park Güell — Gaudí's surreal mosaic hillside park — ideally for the first entry slot (8:00 AM) to enjoy the terraces before crowds arrive. A private guide can bring the symbolism and architecture to life. Afterward, hike or taxi up to the Turó de la Rovira (Bunkers del Carmel) for the most spectacular 360° panoramic view of Barcelona — a hidden gem favored by locals.
day_by_day.afternoon: Casa Milà (La Pedrera) Rooftop & Interior Tour: Descend back into Eixample for a premium guided visit to Casa Milà, known as La Pedrera — Gaudí's extraordinary apartment building with its famous undulating stone facade and iconic warrior-chimney rooftop. The rooftop at golden hour is extraordinary. Explore the Espai Gaudí exhibition inside the attic to understand the architect's genius in depth.
day_by_day.evening: El Born Cocktail Bar Crawl & Late-Night Jazz: Begin the evening with craft cocktails at Paradiso (consistently ranked among the world's best bars — hidden behind a pastrami shop in El Born). Continue to Bar Marsella in the Gothic Quarter, Barcelona's oldest bar dating to 1820. End the night at the Jamboree Jazz Club on Plaça Reial for world-class live jazz in an intimate underground setting.

meals.breakfast: Forn de Sant Jaume on Passeig de Gràcia — a premium Catalan bakery and café serving fresh croissants, pa amb tomàquet, and freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: La Pepita in El Raval or Café de l'Acadèmia in the Gothic Quarter — refined Catalan cuisine in a historic setting with market-fresh seasonal menus
meals.dinner: Nectari Restaurant (Michelin-starred) in Eixample for creative Mediterranean tasting menus, or Alkimia for inventive Catalan cuisine before your evening bar crawl

day_by_day.notes: Park Güell timed tickets must be purchased in advance — the monumental zone fills up quickly in August. La Pedrera offers a special 'Magic Nights' rooftop event in summer with live music and cava — highly recommended if available on this date. Book Paradiso via their online reservation system.

day_by_day.morning: Montjuïc Castle & Fundació Joan Miró: Take the Montjuïc Cable Car (Telefèric de Montjuïc) from Barceloneta for sweeping harbor views on the ascent. Explore the 17th-century Montjuïc Castle with its dramatic panoramas over the city and port. Descend to visit the Fundació Joan Miró — a world-class modern art museum housed in a stunning rationalist building by Josep Lluís Sert, set amid Mediterranean gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely Farewell Lunch & Last-Minute Luxury Shopping: Return to Eixample for a long, indulgent farewell lunch. Spend the remaining afternoon browsing the luxury flagship stores on Passeig de Gràcia — from local designer Custo Barcelona to international maisons. Visit El Corte Inglés' gourmet food hall for premium Catalan souvenirs: cured meats, artisan cheeses, craft gins, and olive oils to take home.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner with Skyline Views & Optional Flamenco Show: Celebrate the final evening with a rooftop dinner or a table at a restaurant with panoramic city views. Optionally, attend a premium flamenco performance at Tablao Flamenco Cordobés or the upscale Palau Dalmases in El Born for an intimate, high-quality show before retiring.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or visit Espai Mescladís — a social enterprise café in Poblenou serving outstanding brunch with a conscience, if time allows for a detour
meals.lunch: Marea Alta at the World Trade Center Barcelona — a premium seafood restaurant with extraordinary panoramic harbor views; the perfect farewell lunch setting
meals.dinner: Azul Restaurant at the W Barcelona hotel for a glamorous final dinner overlooking the sea and city lights, or return to a favorite from earlier in the trip for a sentimental last meal

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if your departure flight is later in the evening. The Montjuïc Cable Car can have queues in August — arrive early or book a private transfer up the hill. Tablao Flamenco Cordobés and Palau Dalmases both require advance reservations for premium seating.
